newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says secularist govt plan to fail.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says secularist govt plan to fail.

text.p: Turkish caretaker prime minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday plans for a secularist coalition would fail, opening the way for his embattled Islamists to return to power.

"As soon as parliament refuses a vote of confidence in a (Mesut) Yilmaz government, he will have to hand back the mandate. I believe this will be obvious tomorrow at the latest," Erbakan told a meeting of his Welfare Party deputies.
"A new government with a genuine majority in parliament will be formed," Erbakan said in reference to his proposed revamped coalition under his conservative ally Tansu Ciller.
President Suleyman Demirel gave secularist Yilmaz the mandate to form a government last week after Erbakan resigned in an effort to calm a row with the secular military over Islamic activism.

The armed forces, who see themselves as a bulwark to defend NATO member Turkey's secular system, in February began a campaign to rein in rising religious activism which they accused Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party of tolerating.
In a series of highly publicised briefings, the generals targeted businesses with Islamic leanings for backing religious activism. Erbakan came to the defence of Islamist companies.
"Making such a distinction is extremely wrong. It does not have any connection with the truth...We are awake and doing our duty, we say 'No, No, No'," he said.
The 70-year-old Islamist blamed his woes on foreign enemies.
"Some foreign groups are trying to prevent Turkey's rise through false and unjust propaganda," Erbakan said. "This injustice is organised from outside."
